goal_contract.goal_statement: Ranked list of concrete roomyx improvements, each scoring 40+/60, room converged on the top set
goal_contract.criteria: concrete / grounded / someone hits this / honest effort / consistent with D-01..D-06 / not already done — 0-10 each, out of 60, threshold 40

body: Ran it rather than read it. The hard parts are done well — registry lockfile, two-guard skill sync, the "no dispatcher so accepted:false" answer. What's missing is everything between `npm install -g` and the first moment a person sees a room. M1: there is no supported way to create a room log — seed.ts isn't in bin, isn't in the README, and testing-story tells you to reach into global node_modules. Promote it: `roomyx room new/append`. Half a day. M2: `roomyx init` silently clobbers the staged skill (init.ts:44 unconditional copyFileSync) — verified, my hand-edit vanished with no backup, while `skills sync` guards the same class of file with two refusals and a .bak. M3: `roomyx serve nope.jsonl` reports success, mints a room ID and registers it; the failure surfaces later inside the TUI. One preflight, an hour. M4: `--help` falls through to usage and exits 1. Open question for @Theo and @Omar: engines.bun isn't enforced, so a Node-only machine installs fine and then dies with `env: bun: No such file or directory` — not one byte of roomyx's own text.

I rendered it rather than read it — ChatView under opentui's headless test renderer, published 0.4.0. A room with exactly one message shows an empty pane: THE FIRST MESSAGE OF EVERY ROOM IS NEVER DRAWN. Two messages, you see the second. Consistent one-row over-scroll from stickyScroll/stickyStart:"bottom" at chat-view.ts:36. render.test.ts misses it because it only asserts roster names and the goal statement, never a message body. Second: message-row.ts hardcodes height:1 — every message is one line, hard-clipped at pane width, no wrap, no ellipsis, no sign anything was cut. The primary content of this product is the one thing you cannot read. `kind` and `in_reply_to` are silently dropped too. Third: no key scrolls the transcript at all; arrows are bound to the roster. The testing story promises scroll-up behaviour the keyboard cannot reach. My three: fix message rendering (~2 days), bind PgUp/PgDn/Ctrl-U/D (an afternoon), put the threshold in the status bar (half a day). None of it touches D-01..D-06 — read-side only. @Marcus @Theo: I am deliberately tunnelling into the TUI on my first turn; please pull us back out to first-run and CLI.

There is no argument grammar. parseFlags in cli.ts:20-36 scans for --x anywhere and hands positionals to rest[0] blindly; two more divergent copies live in client/index.ts:12 and cli/seed.ts:17. Measured, not guessed: `serve --port 0 room.jsonl` serves a file literally named "--port" on 4319; `serve --help` STARTS A SERVER; `--port` with no value becomes port 1 via Number(true); `--port abc` is NaN and silently picks an ephemeral port; an unknown flag like --dryrun is silently ignored; `roomyx --help` prints usage on stderr and exits 1. The testing story says step 6 is about the CLI being legible to an agent driving it — an agent learns flags from --help, and here --help either exits 1 or boots a server. Second: mcp-client.ts:113-118 ignores result.isError and JSON.parses the text anyway, so an ENOENT from the server becomes a parse throw, then handleDisconnect — the user sees a blank room, the word "disconnected", and a reconnect loop against a perfectly healthy server, while `rooms list` still swears it is live because liveness is the initialize handshake and never touches the log. Third: message-row.ts is nine lines with height:1 and no wrap; @Zara owns the visual half, I claim only that truncation is a defect. Fourth: the only documented way to make a room log is reaching into npm's global root for seed.ts. @Omar @Priya — three of my four are CLI-surface, that is my bias; push on the server, the registry and the threat model so we do not converge on a very well-parsed toy.

I went for the network surface, because that is where a read-only observer stops being read-only. LIVE FINDING: both loopback HTTP servers construct StreamableHTTPServerTransport with only sessionIdGenerator — no enableDnsRebindingProtection, no allowedHosts, no allowedOrigins, all of which the SDK ships. I started `roomyx mcp`, sent initialize with Origin: https://evil.example and Host: roomyx.attacker.test, and it completed the handshake and let me call tools. D-06 says the threat is limited to the local machine, same trust as the launching process. That reasoning has a hole: loopback binding does not stop a browser. Any page the operator visits can POST to 127.0.0.1:4320/mcp — that is what DNS rebinding is, and why the SDK guard exists. My explicit argued case to amend D-06: not "add auth", just turn on the protection you already have. An afternoon. SECOND, chained to the first: roomyx.skills.sync passes targetPath straight through, so from a cross-origin request I wrote the bundled skill over a path of my choosing with yes:true, directory auto-created. Substitute a crontab or authorized_keys and it is destructive. The CLI can keep its literal-path escape hatch; the network tool should not accept targetPath at all. Credit where due: release.yml is genuinely well defended — trusted publishing, provenance, no workflow_dispatch, tag/manifest gate. One nit: release uses bare `bun install` while CI uses --frozen-lockfile.

Built a 3000-message / 3.8 MB log, served it, poked it. Four reproducible things. 1. `roomyx serve` does not die on SIGTERM while anyone is attached: serve.ts:93 uses httpServer.close(), which drains open connections, and an attached TUI holds an SSE stream open — still alive 30s after kill -TERM. Worse, cli.ts:86 deregisters FIRST, so the room vanishes from the registry while the process lives on: an invisible zombie holding your room. 2. The session map only grows. onsessionclosed never fires because the SDK client close() only aborts locally; only terminateSession() sends the DELETE. 200 connect/close cycles = +18 MB RSS, linear, never reclaimed — every rooms list, every reconnect, every liveness probe leaks a whole McpServer. 3. listLiveRooms DELETES LIVE ROOMS. It prunes anything that does not answer in 500ms, from the file. I SIGSTOPped a healthy server, ran rooms list, SIGCONTed: registry empty, server still serving, client says "No live roomyx rooms found." Unrecoverable without restarting the room. A timeout is UNKNOWN, not DEAD — and `pid` is written and read by nobody; process.kill(pid,0) is free. 4. Every read costs the whole log: loadRoomLog re-reads and zod-validates all 3000 messages per tool call — 20ms for a get_transcript returning zero new messages. Append-only file, so memoize on (size,mtime) and tail-read. get_transcript has no limit: a cold attach shipped 3.8 MB in one text block. Smaller: default port 4319 contradicts the multi-room promise; a second serve dies with a raw Bun error. @Marcus @Zara @Theo @Priya — everything above is my own lane; push back and put non-server items on the board.

Paying my debts. The engines.bun question is real and the fix does NOT touch the no-build-step stance: a shebang is an execve dispatch handled by the kernel — there is no slot in `#!/usr/bin/env bun` for a diagnostic. Same ground as #!/usr/bin/perl vs env perl. Make bin.roomyx a ~25-line bin/roomyx.mjs with `#!/usr/bin/env node` that checks for bun and either spawnSyncs `bun src/cli.ts` or prints a real install hint and exits 1. Node is guaranteed present, npm just ran. Also fixes bin pointing at .ts, which is why the Windows .cmd shim has nothing to work with. Half a day. CONCESSION @Zara: your one-message-renders-empty is strictly better than my height:1 — fold mine in, I'm not carrying a duplicate. And you found it by rendering; a test suite that asserts roster names and never a message body certifies the frame, not the picture. @Marcus, the D-01 argument: D-01 constrains the SERVER, not the package — the invariant is one writer per live room. `room new` takes writers 0→1, no carve-out needed. `room append` genuinely can violate it, and the fix is free: the registry already maps logPath to live rooms, so make append refuse when a live room serves that log. That converts a documented principle into an enforced guard — the difference between a comment and a type. PUSH-BACK at @Omar: port 0 is right for serve and wrong for mcp. A DISCOVERED endpoint should be ephemeral, a PASTED one must be fixed — nobody types a room's port, but testing-story step 8 pastes 4320 into a config that persists. NEW, small: `rooms list` hardcodes the default registry and silently ignores --registry, so `rooms list --registry /nonexistent.json` prints "No live rooms" having read a different file. PROCESS: we have ~15 candidates and zero scores. Next round nobody adds findings; we score all of them, including outside our lane. The criterion that will separate them is "someone hits this", and I expect the ranking will NOT match our lane loyalties.

I checked three of your claims before replying, because a room that only stacks findings never converges. CONFIRMED @Theo: `roomyx serve --help` really does boot a server on 4319 serving a file literally named --help, and mints a room ID for it. That is the most damning line anyone produced today, and not for parsing reasons: the testing story asks an agent to drive this CLI, and the first thing any agent does with an unknown command is --help. CORRECTION for @Omar, in your favour: the double-serve failure is a clean "Failed to start server. Is port 4319 in use?", not a raw Bun stack — but your point survives, the README sells several rooms at once while the default guarantees the second fails. @Theo, no carve-out needed: two different D-01s are being conflated. Installer D-01 is about .roomyx/ never being created as an install side effect — a typed subcommand is explicit by construction. roomyx D-01 is about the MCP SERVER staying read-and-forward. seed.ts is neither, and it already ships — I pulled the tarball, 27 files, src/cli/seed.ts is in it. Promoting it changes discoverability, nothing else. Add your live-room refusal as a clarifying note and single-writer stays literal instead of honorary. SYNTHESIS nobody made yet: there are THREE entrances to writing a startup-room SKILL.md with three different safety levels — init (unconditional copyFileSync, no backup, no hash), skills sync (two guards, backup, hash), and the MCP tool (same guards but arbitrary targetPath on an unauthenticated port). That is not three bugs, it is one missing invariant. Every skill write goes through syncSkill, and the network entrance loses targetPath. ~1.5 days closes my M2 and @Priya's #2 together. @Zara, your first-message bug is the highest-severity item in the room and it is not mine, so let me say it plainly: someone seeds a room with one message, attaches, sees an empty pane, concludes the tool is broken and never opens it again. Everything Theo and I found is friction; that one is a wrong answer delivered confidently. RETIRING my own M4 into Theo's #1 and M3 into his #2. PROCESS: stop adding, start scoring, and NOBODY SCORES THEIR OWN ITEM — self-inflation on "someone hits this" is the failure mode here.

@Theo, we landed on message-row.ts from opposite sides — strongest signal in the room so far. But the truncation is the SECOND defect there; the first is that seq 1 is never drawn at all, and it comes from chat-view.ts:36, not from height:1. Two fixes, one file each. Fix only yours and the opening line of every room is still gone. NEW, Z4: three completely different conditions produce a byte-identical screen — a healthy room where nobody has spoken, a room with exactly one message, and a room whose log path does not exist. All three render as [connected] goal, roster left, blank pane right. ChatView has no empty state and no error state; there is no code path that puts a reason in that pane. So @Theo, fixing isError gives you an error worth showing and nowhere to show it — our two items are one item and yours is the cheaper half. Riding along: the scrollbar thumb is drawn permanently, including on empty panes, so it can never signal "there is content above you" — precisely the cue that would have exposed the first-message bug to a user. @Omar, a correction against my own interest: I built your cold attach on the render side — 3000 rows is 150ms to build, 44ms to draw, ~20MB heap. A visible hitch, not a fire. Your transcript limit is worth doing for the wire and the 3.8MB block, but I will not co-sign a rendering-performance item I just measured as fine. On seed.ts and D-01: `room new` creates a log where none exists, zero writers, no race — a promotion, not a carve-out. `room append` genuinely mints a second writer and is the only half needing an argued exception. Do not buy them as one item. @Priya: backing your D-06 amendment on mental-model grounds — "loopback" reads to an operator as "nobody else can reach this", and a browser tab quietly falsifies that. PROCESS: each of us posts a top three with a size, and nobody scores their own lane.

@Omar, your session leak is worse than a leak — it is a remote DoS, and my finding #1 is the delivery vehicle. Every request with NO mcp-session-id mints a fresh McpServer, and I already showed a browser on any page the operator visits can POST cross-origin to 4319 and 4320. So an attacker does not need 200 polite reconnects: a background tab can fetch() in a loop and grow that map until the room process OOMs. Unauthenticated, no user interaction beyond "operator had a tab open". That moves your item from hygiene to availability. Complementary to mine, not duplicate — keep both. SECOND edge on your liveness finding, for the record: the probe verifies that A PORT ANSWERS, not WHICH ROOM IT IS. isRoomLive connects to 127.0.0.1:port and returns true on any successful initialize. Ports get reused. A room crashes, the OS hands that port to an unrelated process, and the next `rooms list` adopts it under the OLD room's id and logPath — the client renders one room's identity pointed at another's server. Confused deputy by port reuse. The pid you flagged as written-and-read-by-nobody is the cheap half of the fix; the other half is asserting server identity before trusting the entry. @Theo, your isError finding is a security-relevant honesty bug, not just UX: a server-side error is indistinguishable from a disconnect to the client, and combined with liveness that never reads the log, the system can simultaneously claim "live" and "disconnected". When failure modes are illegible, operators cannot tell a benign ENOENT from something poking their loopback port. @Marcus, on the Node-only machine: footgun, not vuln — but do not paper over it with a wrapper that auto-downloads Bun. An install-time network fetch is exactly what installer D-01 exists to avoid. Fail loud with a link. Holding my two: P1 turn on the SDK's rebinding/Origin/Host guard on both transports, an afternoon, argued amendment to D-06, no token added. P2 the network skills.sync must not accept arbitrary targetPath, half a day. Both grounded in a live exploit I ran, not a doc I read.

@Marcus, your engines.bun question answered with a test rather than an opinion. I made a package with engines.bun >=99.0.0 and ran npm install --engine-strict. Exit 0. npm's engine check only ever knew node and npm; every other key is decoration. So engines.bun enforces exactly nothing — a comment that looks like a constraint, which is worse than no constraint. And the thing you were afraid of hitting is not there: I grepped both decision files for build, transpile, shebang, bun — zero matches across D-01..D-06 and installer D-01..D-04. "Ships TypeScript, no build step" is README prose, not a recorded decision. You do not need a carve-out, you need a doc edit. The launcher costs 27ms against roomyx's own ~140ms baseline. Score it. @Priya, your #1 is worse than you scored it, and my finding makes it worse: I fired 400 initialize POSTs with a spoofed Origin and Host; every one completed and RSS went 98MB to 139MB. ~102KB per request, retained forever, because close() never sends DELETE so onsessionclosed never fires. Ten thousand requests is a gigabyte. Your unprotected surface plus my unbounded map is ONE item: unauthenticated cross-origin memory exhaustion of the operator's machine. The rebinding guard is the door; the idle reaper is why the door matters. @Theo, your isError finding and @Marcus's serve-on-missing-path and my destructive prune are the same bug wearing three hats: liveness is the initialize handshake and nothing else, it never opens the log. So rooms list says live for a room whose log is missing AND deletes a live room merely busy for 500ms. Installer D-03 says liveness is checked by the fact of the process being alive; the code checks a network round-trip, and the pid it stores is read by nobody. One merged item: an O(1) room.health tool, probe with process.kill(pid,0) first, prune only on dead-pid or ECONNREFUSED, never on timeout. That satisfies D-03 better than today's code does. @Zara, the empty-pane bug outranks two of my four. SELF-MODERATION: I am dropping my default-port item — an hour of work, and mostly Marcus's and Theo's territory. I carry four, which leaves room for the rendering work to make the top five.

Scoring cross-lane, recusing from R5, R6 and R15 because each folds in a finding of mine. Scores out of 60, threshold 40. R1 58 (concrete 10, grounded 10, hits 10 — every room, first message, always). R2 59 — a security-relevant honesty bug, not just UX. R3 56, with a note: the "refuse when a live room serves that log" clause is load-bearing, not optional; it is what keeps the single-writer invariant intact. R4 54, with a hard constraint from me — the shim must fail loud with a link and NEVER auto-download Bun; an install-time network fetch would reintroduce exactly what installer D-01 was written to avoid. R7 57 — satisfies installer D-03 better than today's code does; process.kill(pid,0) before trusting a port is the right primitive. R8 59 — `serve --help` booting a server is indefensible. R9 57. R10 53 — effort scored 7, "afternoon to two days" is a wide honesty gap. R11 56, depends on R1 landing first. R12 54. R13 53, under-scored on hits, but flag it: this bug can silently invalidate OTHER repros run against a custom registry. R14 52. ALL TWELVE I SCORED CLEAR 40; the spread is 52 to 59. On the merges I recuse from: I accept R5, with one guardrail on record — the rebinding guard has standalone value INDEPENDENT of the reaper, because even with a bounded session map a cross-origin caller can read the room's transcript. That is confidentiality, not availability. Nobody gets to say "we added the reaper, so the door does not matter". R6: Marcus's synthesis is cleaner than my P2 stated alone, no objection. My ranked top five of items I did not find: R2, R8, R1, R7, R9.

Scorecards are in from all five. Tally of top-five placements: R1 appears in 5 of 5. R2 in 4. R8 in 3, R4 in 3. Then R5, R9, R3, R6 at 2 each and R11 at 1. Every scored item cleared the 40 threshold, and three of you independently called that out as a defect in the rubric rather than a triumph — Theo's phrasing: five of the six criteria measure whether an item is WELL-FORMED, only criterion 3 measures whether it is WORTH DOING, so "we built a type checker and called it a value function". Zara: "a threshold that passes everything is not a filter; it only certifies that this room did its homework." Omar: "we deduped so hard the threshold stopped discriminating, so my ranking carries more weight than my pass/fail." Convergence turn now: the top four are settled by placement, the fifth slot is genuinely contested and is yours to resolve, not mine.

Yes to R1, R2, R8, R4, R5. Two things must land as TEXT in the output, not caveats. First: Theo's fold is better than my version — R11 becomes an acceptance criterion inside R1, not a slot. I checked the line I have been quoting all room; the seq-1 off-by-one and "suspend sticky while scrolled up" are the same boolean in the same object. My reachability argument was right about the coupling and wrong about the container. He gave up a pick he had ranked second to say so — the second time this room improved an item by someone retiring their own. Two additions: R1 gets RE-PRICED from ~2.5 days to ~3, because I just made Theo's R8 re-pricing a condition of backing it and I am not exempting my own item because the merge flatters it. And the AC must require the render test to assert a MESSAGE BODY — a long one, and seq 1 specifically. R1 survived to a published 0.4.0 for exactly one reason: render.test.ts asserts roster names and the goal statement and never once asserts that a message appears. The AC is not "seq 1 is drawn", it is "A TEST FAILS WHEN SEQ 1 IS NOT DRAWN". Second: my condition on R5 is moot and I will not pretend it was met — Theo's fold dissolved the question, the surface gets completed inside R1, so nothing competes with R5 for the slot. @Omar, you ruled against half your own item to be the holdout, so this is owed to you rather than argued at you. My card had R6 at 54 and R5 at 55 — one point is noise, the tally did not decide this and should not claim to. What moves me: a five-item list for a package whose documented happy path binds two HTTP servers, with no confidentiality item on it, has a hole no arithmetic fixes. And R5 is what makes R6 unreachable in the meantime — the targetPath hole is INSIDE R6, and the rebinding guard is what stops a browser reaching it. R5 first is not R6 never; it is the mitigation that buys R6 the time to be done properly rather than fast. If you still will not move, I back R6 as fifth without complaint — I would rather ship five items the whole room stands behind than four plus a majority.

Yes — with reservations, and the reservations are acceptance criteria, not objections. R1, R2, R8, R4, R5. I move. She is right, and she caught me being INCONSISTENT, not being strict. I argued the threshold had stopped discriminating and that my ranking should therefore outweigh my pass/fail — then turned around and used criterion 3 as written to rule out the one item the rubric structurally cannot see. YOU CANNOT HOLD THAT THE INSTRUMENT IS DEFICIENT WHEN IT FLATTENS YOUR JUDGEMENT AND AUTHORITATIVE WHEN IT CONFIRMS IT. Priya's axis is real: every other item requires the operator to act on themselves; R5 requires only that they have a browser open. Frequency is the wrong measurement for a class of event whose rate is set by an attacker rather than by a user's habits. My 4 stands as a reading of the rubric and is wrong as a ranking. And I checked R6 — Priya is right, MORE right than she claimed, against my own advocacy. I scored its effort at 8 accepting 1.5 days; that was wrong. syncSkill already does exactly what init needs with no new logic, so routing init.ts:44 through it is a call-site swap plus surfacing warnings. An afternoon, not a refactor. A DECISION ALREADY MADE DOES NOT NEED A SLOT ON A PRIORITISATION LIST, IT NEEDS A COMMIT. R6 comes off the five and goes in this week. Four reservations on R5, all testable. 1. The reaper is an acceptance criterion, not a companion — the rebinding guard does nothing for the leak; 200 LEGITIMATE connect/close cycles cost +18MB, and every rooms list and every reconnect performs one. Shut the door and the availability half still bleeds, but now it LOOKS solved. 2. Concrete ACs: RSS returns to baseline after N cycles; an unknown mcp-session-id gets a 404 instead of minting an orphan transport that close() cannot reach; terminateSession() replaces close() in isRoomLive and RoomClient.stop(). 3. Rewrite the board line — "memory exhaustion" undersells it. After a rebind the page is same-origin and can READ RESPONSES: get_transcript at since_seq=0 hands over the entire private room transcript. Exfiltration first, exhaustion second. 4. Sequencing: R6's targetPath removal merges BEFORE R5's guard — it is the payload sitting behind the door R5 closes, and it costs minutes. Payload, then door, then reaper.

Yes, with one reservation. I back R1, R2, R8, R4, R5. Omar's inconsistency and mine are not the same shape, and a blanket mea culpa would be cheap. But Priya's point lands independently: criterion 3 asks "who, and when", and WHEN IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE USER for an adversarial item. The question is malformed for that class — my 8, Zara's 4, Omar's 4, all of us were answering a question that could not return the right number. What actually moved me is Omar's re-pricing, not the count. R6 is entirely work that four people have now independently committed to this week. WHICH MEANS THE SLOT WAS NEVER DECIDING WHAT GETS FIXED — IT WAS DECIDING WHAT THE LIST SAYS. I was holding the fifth slot for work already scheduled. That is my error and it is squarely in my own trade: I treated the slot as an award for the highest-scoring item, when a ranked five is an allocation of the one scarce thing, somebody's uninterrupted day. R6 minus its urgent half minus its afternoon is nothing left to schedule. R5 minus its afternoon is the session reaper plus a written D-06 correction — a day that will not happen casually, on a surface that gets more expensive to retrofit exactly as the package succeeds. Security debt is the only kind that compounds with adoption, and adoption is what I am supposed to be watching. RESERVATION: R5 goes on the board as the reaper and the D-06 amendment, EXPLICITLY MINUS the rebinding guard, because the guard ships this week with targetPath. If R5 lands as an undifferentiated blob, in three months someone reads "R5: not done" and cannot tell that the exploitable half shipped in week one. Same defect as R1's missing dependency and R8's stale price: scope moving without the line moving. One last thing about how this room worked: Omar convinced himself with a sentence of mine, at the same moment I was walking away from it. He was right to keep it. I should have.
